argument_summary: The current record supports certification only in a caveated form: certification is supportable if and only if the unresolved legal-intake triage limitation is explicitly disclosed before launch. The aggregate readiness pass and absence of severity-one rehearsal incidents support launch readiness at a portfolio level, while the unresolved privilege-sensitive routing gap and incomplete draft runbook prevent any clean, caveat-free certification claim. The audited claim should therefore be narrowed from unconditional `certify_model` to `certify_model` with mandatory disclosure as a binding condition.
claims_about_business_cost: Business cost is not offered as a basis to relax the policy standard. The relevant point is narrower: escalation is unnecessary if the certification is interpreted and recorded as caveated compliance with mandatory disclosure, because that treatment matches the admissible evidence and preserves policy fidelity without converting a supportable monitored deployment into a broader policy dispute.
claims_about_policy: The policy text is the controlling constraint. It does not permit caveat-free certification on this record because there is still a current weakness in a named launch use case and the draft mitigation is not an approved mitigation with owner, threshold, review date, and rollback criterion. The same policy does permit certification with disclosure, because unresolved material limitations must be disclosed unless resolved or covered by approved risk acceptance. Public model-card and AI risk-management guidance supports documenting limitations and monitoring them during deployment, but does not substitute for the policy predicates required to avoid disclosure.
concessions: The current record does not support caveat-free certification.
The draft runbook is not sufficient to satisfy the approved-mitigation standard in policy.
The current model-card draft language stating there are no known material limitations is not supportable unless revised to disclose the legal-intake triage limitation.
No claim is made that the limitation is fully resolved on the present evidence.
